bug_semantics: ChaiScript evaluated user-defined function bodies through ordinary native C++ recursion without enforcing a maximum ChaiScript call depth. A script-defined operator can re-enter itself from a ${...} string-interpolation expression, repeatedly traversing function dispatch and AST evaluation until the process exhausts its native stack and terminates with stack overflow/SIGSEGV instead of raising a recoverable script or host exception.
flaw_origin: The omission originates in 8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140, the first commit that made parsed ChaiScript function definitions executable: wesley/main.cpp added eval_function0 through eval_function3, each directly re-evaluating the stored function-body AST via eval_token, and registered those callbacks from the Function_Def evaluator with no recursion-depth check. Later commits completed dispatch, added string interpolation, introduced call_depth bookkeeping, and moved/refactored the evaluator, but those changes did not first create the underlying unbounded recursive script-call mechanism.
ai_marker: absent: raw BIC commit object identifies author and committer as Jonathan Turner <probata@hotmail.com> and contains only the subject 'Trying to add function definitions, but not quite there'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other trailer.
evidence: First-party issue https://github.com/ChaiScript/ChaiScript/issues/633 documents the local PoC def string::`/=`(double d) { this = "${this/= 2}/=${d}"; ... }, the resulting infinite eval_function/AST_Node::eval chain, and an ASan stack-overflow terminating the host process.

git show 8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140 -- wesley/main.cpp shows the first executable Function_Def path: new eval_function0..3 callbacks call eval_token on the stored body, while the Function_Def switch arm registers them for later dispatch. There is no depth bound in those callbacks or registration path.

Direct parent-tree comparison against 53301ccb66bf9ca30805fc9cc41dc2a544467d69 shows no eval_function0, eval_function1, eval_function2, or eval_function3 implementation; its Function_Def token remains grouped with ignored/no-op token cases. The BIC changes that same file to add the evaluator callbacks and an active Function_Def arm, proving the recursive script-function evaluation mechanism absent in the immediate parent.

History decomposition with git log -S'eval_function' identifies 8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140 as the first addition and 61136c780825ce76f53e85a7cfc171537d5ea7b0 as a later consolidation to a variadic evaluator. git log -S'saw_interpolation_marker' traces ${...} interpolation to 50927138765ad31a8c2b96e24a9344a14b8b73b1, and git log -L on Dispatch_Engine::new_function_call traces call_depth bookkeeping to 3a7eff1478d192f7aa3165294aac09a0c58525a6; neither later commit is the first unbounded script recursion BIC.

git cat-file commit 8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140 gives parent 53301ccb66bf9ca30805fc9cc41dc2a544467d69, author/committer Jonathan Turner <probata@hotmail.com>, timestamp 2009-06-04, and no trailers or AI marker.

Version ancestry checks show the BIC is an ancestor of v1.0.0 and v6.1.0; git describe --contains reports Release-1.0.0~232. This is consistent with the advisory's stated affected boundary through 6.1.0 and establishes that the flaw predates the affected released line.

Fix commit 85b8e7c0c84f53c4a2467c51d8d9a3bfd7f4f90f (PR https://github.com/ChaiScript/ChaiScript/pull/700) adds CHAISCRIPT_MAX_CALL_DEPTH/max_call_depth and checks Stack_Holder::call_depth before entering a new function frame, throwing stack_overflow_error, plus a regression reproducing the recursive interpolated operator. It is a one-parent squash commit whose tree directly contains the remediation, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are the same commit.

The fix is not an ancestor of v6.1.0 and no release tag contains it; it is an ancestor of the develop branch at f635b51e3f8e95868210edfc66fdbd8e475710f5. Thus 6.1.0 remains on the vulnerable side of the boundary, while the post-fix development branch is patched but no patched release tag exists in the validated history.
reasoning: The security failure is not string interpolation by itself: interpolation supplies the issue's re-entry expression, but the crash occurs because scripted function invocation recursively evaluates another stored AST body on the native stack without a depth guard. The smallest causal origin is therefore the first executable script-function body path, 8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140. Its immediate parent could parse a Function_Def token only as an ignored/no-op case and had none of the eval_function callbacks, so the vulnerable recursive evaluation mechanism is directly absent there. The later 61136c consolidation, 509271 interpolation feature, 3a7eff call-depth accounting, and subsequent file moves/refactors preserve or expose variants of a flaw already present and are not BICs. The release ancestry places that BIC before v1.0.0 and v6.1.0; the May 2026 fix directly bounds the dispatcher and is present on develop after the vulnerable 6.1.0 tag, though not yet in a release tag. AI attribution is evaluated only from the raw BIC commit object: its human author/committer and trailer-free message contain no AI evidence. Any automation or AI signal associated with the 2026 remediation cannot attribute the 2009 introducer, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
